title: Post-call: target cost buckets and competitive comparison vs hosts
text:
Post-call: target cost buckets and competitive comparison vs hosts

["From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>\\nTo: Emma Cole <emma@finvantage.com>\\nCc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>\\nDate: Thu, 19 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700\\nSubject: Post-call recap: target cost buckets + benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic\\n\\nHi Emma — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our call and the asks we agreed on so we can move toward procurement. I captured the key points below and included next steps.\\n\\nSummary of what you shared\\n- Monthly active inference: initial pilot ~150M tokens/mo, scale target 450–600M tokens/mo in 3–6 months.\\n- Latency requirement: ~ <400ms p95 for chat workflows; occasional batch jobs for async summarization.\\n- Quality bar: current eval set needs >92% intent/safety pass rate.\\n- Budget posture: finance gave a ballpark committed budget of $40k–$60k/mo for production; procurement asked us for a target $/1M token rate to compare against incumbent hosts.\\n\\nCamila's suggested cost buckets (we can firm these with an internal price review)\\n- Tier A (pilot): 150–250M tokens/mo — target $/1M = $16–$20 (short-term, higher overhead for smaller pools)\\n- Tier B (growth): 250–500M tokens/mo — target $/1M = $10–$14 (reserved capacity + modest commit)\\n- Tier C (scale): 500M+ tokens/mo — target $/1M = $6–$9 (deep commit + quantization/optimizations)\\n\\nBenchmark note (high-level):\\n- OpenAI/Anthropic (public comparables): commonly quoted in our fieldwork at mid-teens per 1M tokens for chat-heavy workloads if you need latest safety models; Anthropic sometimes slightly lower depending on model choice.\\n- Open-model hosts (self-hosting/open-host services): big variance — cheaper at scale if you can accept quantized variants and slightly higher latency; ranges we see $5–$12/1M depending on architecture and GPU share.\\n\\nAttachments: I attached an initial cost model workbook that converts your monthly token ranges into total monthly spend across different tiering/commit assumptions (redwood-initial-cost-model.xlsx). Also attached a short scope summary (finvantage-scope-summary.pdf).\\n\\nImmediate asks / next steps\\n1) Can you confirm the 450–600M tokens/mo scale target is the committee target for Q4? If not, give a more precise midpoint we should model.\\n2) Procurement asked whether Redwood can do a draft SOW + standard enterprise T&Cs and a preliminary rate card for Tier B and Tier C — should I put those in a DocuSign-ready packet?\\n3) If acceptable, we’ll model two price ladders: (A) short-term promotional credit for first 2 months (applied to pilot), (B) commit-based ladder to hit $6–$9/1M at 500M+.\\n\\nHappy to jump on a follow-up with procurement next week; propose Tue 08/24 or Wed 08/25.\\n\\nThanks — Camila\\nCamila Reyes\\nEnterprise Sales, Redwood Inference\\ncamila@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192\\n\\n--- attachment: redwood-initial-cost-model.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)\\n--- attachment: finvantage-scope-summary.pdf (application/pdf)", 'From: Emma Cole <emma@finvantage.com>\\nTo: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>\\nDate: Fri, 20 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Post-call recap: target cost buckets + benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic\\n\\nThanks Camila — this is super helpful and aligned with our notes. A few quick clarifications from our side:\\n\\n1) Volume: the 450–600M tokens/mo is our internal stretch target for Q4; our procurement baseline for negotiations will be modeled on ~500M tokens/mo.\\n2) Budget: finance is comfortable modeling up to $50k/mo committed for a first-year deal, but preference is to keep unit economics near $8–$12/1M tokens if possible once we hit 400–500M.\\n3) Competitors: procurement has a memo that lists OpenAI and Anthropic as first comparables; they also asked to see pricing from open-host providers (replicate/hf stones) for a like-for-like quantized variant.\\n\\nCan you do two things: (A) run the attached workbook against a 500M tokens/mo baseline and show the delta to $8/1M vs $12/1M and (B) confirm what Redwood would require (commit term, SLA) to reach $8/1M at 500M.\\n\\nWe are happy to take the draft SOW + T&Cs — please put the packet into DocuSign when ready and cc procurement (procurement@finvantage.com).\\n\\nAppreciate the fast follow-up — Emma\\nEmma Cole\\nHead of Product, FinVantage\\nemma@finvantage.com\\n\\nOn Thu, Aug 19, 2026 at 2:05 PM Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com> wrote:\\n> [original message pasted above]\\n', 'From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>\\nTo: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>\\nCc: Emma Cole <emma@finvantage.com>, FinVantage Procurement <procurement@finvantage.com>\\nDate: Sat, 21 Aug 2026 08:42:00 -0700\\nSubject: RE: Post-call recap: target cost buckets + benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic\\n\\nLooping in Rishi to confirm commercial levers we can use. Quick internal note for the packet we will send:\\n\\n- To hit the lower bound ($8/1M at 500M) we will likely need a 12–18 month committed reservation with a 30–40% prepaid portion or Minimum Commitment Level to justify dedicated pools and deeper packing (this reduces overhead and allows quantized variants in the tail).\\n- Alternative (lower friction): a 6–12 month commit with a blended ladder that starts at ~$12/1M and drops to ~$8/1M once the 500M threshold is hit for two consecutive months.\\n- We should push optional add-ons: extended observability retention, audit logs, and dedicated on-call support (those are common procurement asks and justify margin).\\n\\nRishi — can you (1) populate the rate-card lines (Pilot / Growth / Scale) into the workbook and (2) draft a short comment for procurement that explains typical SLA/credit terms tied to latency SLOs? I’ll assemble the DocuSign packet and proposed SOW.\\n\\nThanks — Marissa\\nMarissa Cole\\nHead of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference\\nmarissa_cole@redwood.com\\n\\n--- internal: reference to HubSpot deal FD-3491\\n', 'From: Procurement FinVantage <procurement@finvantage.com>\\nTo: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>\\nDate: Sat, 21 Aug 2026 10:32:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Post-call recap: target cost buckets + benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic\\n\\nCamila / Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Procurement confirms: please proceed with a DocuSign packet that contains\\n- Draft SOW (scope + initial pilot milestones)\\n- Rate card for Pilot/Growth/Scale with the two ladder options we discussed (6–12mo blended ladder and 12–18mo deep commit)\\n- Standard enterprise T&Cs and an estimate of any onboarding credits/promotional offsets for month 1–2.\\n\\nWe note FinVantage preference for a target of $8–$10/1M once 500M sustained usage is reached. Please include an appendix that summarizes how Redwood’s pricing compares to OpenAI/Anthropic and a short paragraph on what tradeoffs (latency, model freshness, KV caching) lead to the delta vs open-host pricing.\\n\\nProcurement is ready to review the DocuSign packet next week. Please cc procurement@finvantage.com when the packet is ready.\\n\\n— Procurement, FinVantage\\n\\nOn Fri, Aug 20, 2026 at 9:18 AM Emma Cole <emma@finvantage.com> wrote:\\n> [response pasted above]\\n']
